fields.description:
ADR settling what ADR 0050 deferred: how a self-contained rebar MCP HTTP server runs on the
AWS box (Gerrit + review-bot + opcert), so copilot/codex/claude can drive ALL rebar operations
through it (dogfooding). Output: one accepted ADR under docs/adr/ + an ADR 0079 amendment. This
ticket writes only the decision record; the infra/autodeploy/secrets/guidance slices implement
it. No code, infra, AWS, or Jira mutation here.

## Decisions (settled with the operator 2026-08-24)

### 1. Exposure + auth — nginx `/mcp/` TLS edge + `static` verifier + per-client bearer PATs
Loopback-bound `rebar-mcp` HTTP (`transport=http`, `http_tls_at_edge=true`, allowed hosts/origins
set, `auth_resource_server_url` set) behind an nginx `/mcp/` TLS-terminating location — the
documented `docs/mcp-auth.md` §5 recipe, mirroring opcert's TLS edge. Verifier mode = **static**;
each client (copilot/codex/claude) presents its own bearer PAT in the `Authorization` header.
Rationale + prior art: research confirmed all three clients support a static
`Authorization: Bearer <token>` header for remote HTTP MCP and none require OAuth, so `static` is
the minimal mode that satisfies all three clients. This is a **standard self-contained rebar MCP server** (operator
intent: analogous to a user MCP install), NOT the opcert SigV4/API-Gateway `proxy` pattern.
Records the ADR-0050-required non-loopback-bind + TLS-at-edge acknowledgements.

### 2. Autodeploy drain — blue-green immutable-release, modeled on the LOCAL main-tracking updater
The MCP autodeploy target does NOT copy the review-bot's stop-and-health-drain (`docker compose
up -d` + `/health` in_flight gate). It follows the local `origin/main`-tracking updater
(`~/.local/bin/rebar-dev-update.sh`, ticket sticky-genetic-narwhal): immutable release + atomic
pointer swap + retire-when-idle. Concretely on the box (docker): build the new image → start a
NEW `rebar-mcp` container → health-check it → **atomically flip the nginx `/mcp/` upstream** to it
(the `current`-pointer rename analog) → **retire the old container off the critical path**, gated
by a flock-style "still serving?" check (active connections / its own in_flight), with bounded
retention + a hard cap + an SNS alert when a busy old container cannot be reclaimed. Overlap is
capped **one-in / one-out** (never N parallel) and guarded by a memory-pressure alarm so the
transient 2× `rebar-mcp` never forces the t4g.large (8 GiB) up to t4g.xlarge.

Positive rationale (why this over the review-bot pattern): it eliminates the review-bot's unsolved
saturation gotcha (bug 7b4a) — a shared MCP server driven by N agents pipelines long billable LLM
ops so `in_flight` may never reach 0; a gauge-gated bound would then be exhausted and kill an
in-flight certified op, and a bigger bound only defers the same kill. Blue-green decouples
retirement from the deploy, so a never-idle server never blocks a deploy or forces a kill. In-place
reload is rejected outright because rebar lazy-imports late (e.g. `commit_impact` during `close`,
after the minutes-long completion verifier), so swapping code under a running process risks an
ImportError mid-op (two real local incidents). A killed MCP op is client-visible (dropped HTTP
connection → the agent retries), and rebar's event-sourced writes are idempotent (an unpersisted
op-cert is simply re-requested), so retirement is safe.

The `in_flight` gauge counts only long-running / certified / LLM ops (review_plan,
verify_completion, review_code, scan_spec — 30 s to minutes); trivial sub-second reads are not
counted (killing them is harmless, the client retries). The gauge is used for the RETIRE check,
not to gate the deploy.

### 3. Certified-op routing — register the box as a trusted signing environment; code review stays the Gerrit vote
For plan-review + completion-verifier certs minted via MCP to be enforceable, the box must be a
registered trusted signing environment: provision its opcert signing key and pin its pubkey in
`.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml` on `main`, with `verify.require_environment` on (per ADR 0049).
rebar issues exactly TWO op-cert kinds (plan-review at claim, completion-verifier at close, ADR
0049); there is **no code-review op-cert**. "Certified code review" = the existing Gerrit
`LLM-Review` bot vote already on the box — NO new op-cert kind is introduced. The opcert
job-service + `remote-cert` client are left coexisting (additive, not replaced). The epic's item-7
wording ("code review ... certified through the MCP server") is corrected accordingly in the
guidance slice.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A new `docs/adr/00NN-mcp-on-box.md` exists with status **Accepted**, deciding all three items above with the stated rationale, and cross-referencing ADR 0049 (two op-certs), ADR 0050 (RS-only, static verifier, deferred AWS recipe now filled), ADR 0079 (autodeploy), and the local main-tracking updater precedent (sticky-genetic-narwhal). Checked: `test -f docs/adr/*mcp-on-box*.md` and `grep -i 'Status: Accepted'` in it.
- [ ] ADR 0079 carries an amendment describing the `mcp` blue-green pointer-swap target (immutable release + atomic nginx-upstream flip + retire-when-idle), explicitly contrasted with the review-bot stop-and-drain and noting the bug-7b4a saturation rationale. Checked: `grep -i 'mcp\|blue-green' docs/adr/0079-autodeploy-on-box-timer.md`.
- [ ] The ADR names the concrete config keys the infra slice sets (`transport`, `http_tls_at_edge`, allowed hosts/origins, `auth_resource_server_url`, verifier `static`) and the trusted-env keys (`.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml`, `verify.require_environment`). Checked: `grep` the new ADR for each named key.
- [ ] No behavioral code/infra change lands under this ticket. Checked: `git diff --stat` on the change shows only `docs/adr/` paths.

## Testing
Tier: **documentation** — an ADR/decision record with no runtime behavior, so the oracle is the record itself. Verification is by file inspection + `grep` exactly as named in each acceptance item above: the ADR file exists with `Status: Accepted`, contains the three decisions with the named config/trusted-env keys and the four ADR cross-references, the ADR 0079 amendment text is present, and `git diff --stat` shows only `docs/adr/` touched. No automated test tier applies (no code path changes); a lower tier is insufficient because there is nothing executable to assert.

Blocks every implementation slice (infra, autodeploy, secrets, client-config, guidance,
trusted-env registration, live verification).
